messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate for customer 'PolarisBank' on private VPC deployment (vpc-priv-22). Symptom: 502/503 from ALB -> backend NLB healthchecks failing. Impact: session establishment failures for tenant traffic. Page: SRE on-call.
Alex (sre-oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledging pager. Starting initial triage. Any recent deploys? Priya, did we push anything to dedicated pools?
Priya (plat-ops): No deploys to Polaris dedicated pool in the last 24h. Console shows steady config — last change was a routing policy tweak two days ago.
Maya (neteng): Seeing a surge of TCP resets from the NLBs in us-east-1 for vpc-priv-22. Healthchecks are flapping. Could be SG or a backend node failing to accept connections.
Jordan (infra-oncall): Jumping in. Which listeners are affected? ALB -> target group forwarding to NLB? Need to confirm flow.
Alex (sre-oncall): Polaris private setup: external ALB (ingress) -> target group forwarding to NLBs in customer subnets (egress/egress-proxy path). NLBs then route to tenant GP instances in dedicated pool.
Sam (CS-PolarisBank): Customer reporting intermittent failures on their payment endpoints. They've escalated to 1-hour SLA. They are in a live peak window. Happy to coordinate any network changes but please call out customer-visible steps.
Maya (neteng): I pulled NLB health logs. 3/5 targets in tg-pol-22 showing ‘‘connection refused’. Sample: 
```
2026-03-15T14:20:03Z target_id=i-0abcd1234 status=unhealthy reason=ConnRefused
2026-03-15T14:20:10Z target_id=i-0abcd1234 status=unhealthy reason=ConnRefused
```
Also seeing increased RTTs to KMS endpoint that some services call during session init. Could be upstream egress blocking.
Lukas (secops): Checking SG changes now. Last automated security policy run at 2026-03-15T02:00. No manual SG edits listed, but there is a time-windowed rule that expired today which reopens port 443 to specific management CIDRs — unusual to expire.
Jordan (infra-oncall): Running quick connectivity tests from a healthy tenant host to the backend ports (443/8443).
Jordan (infra-oncall): Output: 
```
# from healthy-host in same AZ
$ curl -v https://10.0.12.45:8443/health
* Connected to 10.0.12.45 (10.0.12.45) port 8443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
Jordan (infra-oncall): From a host routed via the NLB we see connection refused. So it's path-specific: ALB->NLB->backend failing, internal hosts can reach backend.
Alex (sre-oncall): Hypothesis: NLB is failing to establish connections to backend because of a security-group egress rule or an ACL blocking traffic originating from NLB ENIs. Suggest we confirm ENI security groups and NACLs for the subnet.
Maya (neteng): Confirmed: NLB ENIs are in subnet-priv-az1 with SG nlb-sg-22. That SG has an egress policy tightened to allow only 10.0.0.0/16 and 172.16.0.0/12 for a maintenance window earlier. That rule was mistakenly added to deny outbound to the tenant port range except for a maintenance CIDR. It looks like the rule had higher priority and is rejecting the traffic.
Priya (plat-ops): Oof. That matches change logs: a templated SG update applied during a template migration. It should not have applied to customer vpc-priv-22. Rolling back now.
deploy-bot: Initiating rollback of security group nlb-sg-22 -> applying previous template (sg-template-v3). Request id: dpl-33221.
Alex (sre-oncall): While rollback is in progress, we should put a targeted mitigation: add a permissive egress rule on the NLB SG to allow 10.0.12.0/24:8443/443 to bypass. Lukas, can you approve the exception? This is customer-impacting.
Lukas (secops): Approving emergency exception for nlb-sg-22 to allow outbound 443,8443 to tenant CIDR 10.0.12.0/24 for 30 minutes. Add an audit annotation.
Maya (neteng): Patch applied: added egress allow rule 10.0.12.0/24 ports 443,8443. On healthchecks now.
Jordan (infra-oncall): Healthcount: from 0/5 to 3/5 1m after patch. Traffic is starting to flow.
Sam (CS-PolarisBank): Customer confirming partial recovery — some requests now succeed. They're still seeing errors on some nodes. They want an ETA for full restoration.
Alex (sre-oncall): Good. We're continuing rollback of the inadvertent SG template. Once rollback completes we will remove the emergency rule and verify healthchecks remain stable. ETA for rollback: ~5-8 minutes.
Priya (plat-ops): Rollback success. sg-template-v3 restored to nlb-sg-22. Removing emergency exception in 2 minutes to validate correct state.
Maya (neteng): Removing exception now.
Jordan (infra-oncall): Healthchecks remain stable at 5/5. No further ConnRefused. Latency normalized.
Sam (CS-PolarisBank): Customer reports full recovery. They are monitoring for the next 15 minutes. Thank you.
Alex (sre-oncall): Root cause: templated SG change mistakenly applied to customer NLB SG during template migration. Contributing factor: time-windowed rule expiry and insufficient scoping in template selector. Action items: (1) block template apply against customer-managed SGs until granular selector fix (Priya), (2) add preflight check to detect permissive constraints on egress that would affect NLB->backend flows (Maya), (3) add an audit alarm when SG changes affect private customer vpcs (Lukas/Priya).
Priya (plat-ops): I'll open infra-ticket INFRA-4629 for the template selector fix and mark it P1 for the dedicated/private flows.
Maya (neteng): I'll follow up with a config rule to reject SG templates that change NLB egress unless explicitly allowed.
Lukas (secops): I'll add an alert to the policy monitoring for SG changes in customer VPCs.
Alex (sre-oncall): Final notes: customer impact was ~22 minutes from first page to full recovery. Incident led to degraded traffic to PolarisBank during peak. We used emergency SG exception and rollback as mitigations. Logging and playbook updated. Sam — we'll follow up with a post-incident summary and RCA within 24h.
Sam (CS-PolarisBank): Appreciate the quick response. Please include timeline and action items in RCA.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED (severity: P1 -> mitigated). Incident ticket IN-98765 closed for now; will reopen if regressions detected.
Alex (sre-oncall): I'll post the initial timeline and add the participants to the incident doc. Closing thread for live updates; keep monitoring for 1h and report any reoccurrences here. :white_check_mark:
